text.p: These are the leading stories in Skopje press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- Macedonians well aware of huge increase of drug abuse in the country, poll by Data Press agency showed. Of 2,800 pollees, 95 percent knew of this but 70 percent denied any acquaintance with drug abusers, 37.23 think reasons for drug abuse are economic and political, also fear of future.
- Macedonian students at Skopje Teachers' academy to boycott classes from February 17 to 21, protesting at Albanian language classes law passed by parliament last Thursday.

- Depositors with blocked savings in several private banks whose managers have disappeared will stage protests in front of the government on Wednesday. Over 30 million German Marks worth of savings blocked.
- Bitola drama theatre to visit Australia and give 18 performances throughout the country.
- Final decision on integration between Liberal and Democratic parties will be made at Democratic Party congress in March, DP leader Petarm Cosev said.
- Rector of illegal Tetovo university Fadil Sulejmani released from prison two months before expiration of his sentence. Sulejmani was sentenced to 12 months in prison for "calling to resistance".
